entries.operation_fingerprint: Use original SideStore Team.account.appleID and Account.isActiveAccount relationship plus native AuthManager currentAppleID to determine selected account and team. Pin both immutable strings across device install, managed slot listing/update, refresh query and host bootstrap; fail closed on owner mismatch even where Team identifier alone matches.
entries.source_behavior_contract: Each Apple ID owns its own Team and managed app records; installation and refresh can touch only exact Account+Team owned rows. Switching B never transfers or mutates A apps or Scarlet host signed Team; no Apple entitlement spoof, global certificate overwrite, app deletions, or shared slot ownership inferred from Team alone.

novelty.causal_difference: P68 and P75 gate active Team ID but never compare SideStore CoreData Team.account appleID; this allows same-Team distinct Apple IDs to see or change each others records and makes install callback ownership ambiguous. The original persisted Team.account relationship is now used in every operation.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: A and B each see only their own managed app rows and install/readback validates both account and Team. A same-Team different-AppleID app is blocked from B refresh and slot actions, without re-signing host or revoking certificates.

new_device_evidence.observed_value: Selected Team 0 targets then manually selected 1 target; P89 uses only team relationship in native worker

novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: Earlier source changes applied only Team ID filtering or host origin; neither enforced installed-app CoreData Team.account.appleID equality or post-install callback ownership confirmation.

after: - User requirement: Apple ID A and Apple ID B MUST be independently owned identities, not a shared permission switch. Device P89 current launch `022f7fbc` (source `c667fa3cd4b1`) shows account switching verified and one selected-Team P12 import, but guest `certificate_invalid`/`signature_postcheck_invalid`, auto refresh selectedTeam no-app and manual refresh install-unverified. These remain unresolved, not CI successes.

- Original SideStore CoreData has `InstalledApp.team -> Team.account -> Account.appleID`, plus `Team.isActiveTeam` and `Account.isActiveAccount`; P68/P75/P89 only filtered by Team ID, which cannot distinguish two Apple IDs sharing a Developer Team. P90 instead pins both authenticated `AuthManager.currentAppleID` AND native active Team relationship under SideStore gate for IPA install, managed slots, refresh and original signed-host bootstrap.

- Native install callback must read back the same `InstalledApp.team.account.appleID` plus `Team.identifier` before claiming pipeline success. No cross-account activate/deactivate, auto-switch, app deletion, revocation, transfer, or rewriting signed host authority. Identity unavailable => fail closed. Existing signed Scarlet host stays with its original Team, even if B is selected.

- P90 code changes scoped to `ScarletGuestSavedAccounts.swift.txt`, `ScarletDeviceInstallAgent.swift.txt`, `ScarletGuestRefreshAgent.swift.txt`, tests and workflow only. P89 native account UI untouched; P89 SideStore per-Team P12 import untouched.

- P90 static acceptance uses two Apple IDs even when Developer Team is the same; static tests cannot substitute for iOS27.2 device signing, installed-app per-owner lists or user screenshot. Check A->B->A and app-slot, native install, per-owner refresh.

entries.action: P90 binds AppManager installed app ownership to native SideStore Team.account relation and supports append-only full-history merging for audit and iPhone log.
entries.observation: Local Linux source tests: 861 run, 3 infra skips. Prior to append test one coverage test blocked missing L149; with append should pass. Xcode CI and user iPhone A/B isolation not verified.
entries.evidence: P89 session 022f7fbc and exact original SideStore Account->Team->InstalledApp relationships; source commit receipt.
entries.next_executable_action: Xcode27.2 native compile and IPA publish, then signed iPhone A-B-A verification of per-account app ownership and manual/automatic refresh.
entries.repeat_policy: Never rely only on Developer Team ID or silently transfer signed-host ownership; keep intact P89 signing baseline.

entries.operation_fingerprint: On a kernel signature postcheck failure, obtain the uniquely owned same-host-team active CertificateManager archive via authenticated original SideStore XPC instead of legacy generic Keychain, then pass to existing crash-safe kernel postcheck transaction.
entries.source_behavior_contract: Only when exactly one saved Apple ID is active and uniquely owns the installed signed host Team, retrieve its existing native SideStore P12 over authenticated XPC; recheck owner after XPC, validate PKCS12 Team and distinctness, run original P78 reversible trial, fail closed and roll back if signature is rejected.

novelty.causal_difference: P78 only queried fixed legacy generic Keychain service items and found no alternate certificate for the P90 device. P89 installed per-account certificates into SideStore CertificateManager, which P78 never inspected. P91 adds the authenticated native CertificateManager retrieval route restricted by account+team owner, while preserving P78 reversible kernel verification.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: P91 on-device native fallback only starts if original same-host-team legacy candidate is absent; with unique active host-team owner and distinct native P12 it begins one kernel-verified reversible trial, whereas missing/cross-team/same-Team multi-owner candidates do not modify LC signing state and no invalid signature is accepted.

new_device_evidence.observed_value: P90 session 93bd3576 had 3 guest signing errors, 3 signature postcheck invalid results, per-account P12 import success for B, no P78 signer_recovery_trial_started; P78 legacy candidate unavailable path is not proven as log omitted its completion.

novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: P78 only queried generic Keychain service and could not reach P89 per-account original SideStore CertificateManager. P89 saves certificates but does not automatically hand a verified host-team candidate into LC guest signing transaction. P90 only enforces app ownership without fixing this certificate store gap.

after: // P91: the original SideStore CertificateManager is NOT the legacy
// generic Keychain service that P78 searched. The native archive is
// fetched only for one unambiguous active Apple ID that owns the signed
// host team, never for an arbitrary selected second account.
// A and B remain independent even when Apple assigned the SAME
// Developer Team. Without a unique owner we cannot infer who owns
// this installed host from its Team entitlement alone.
// Read the REAL SideStore active CertificateManager archive via
// existing on-device XPC; do not create/revoke Apple certificates.
// Reuse P78's transaction, kernel readback and exact rollback;
// only the certificate origin is different, not the sign method.

### L150 · P91 원본 SideStore CertificateManager 기반 게스트 서명 복구 (2026-11-17)

- 2026-11-17 08:29 KST P90 실기기 로그(빌드 3.8.90, SourceCommit `9a3ded62e0f1`, session `93bd3576`): `certificate_preflight`의 P12·서명호스트 팀 일치와 AppGroup 통과에도 실제 게스트 3회 `certificate_invalid` / `signature_postcheck_invalid`; A/B 전환 성공, 계정별 P12 가져오기 성공, 자동 갱신 선택 팀의 관리 앱 수는 0. 이는 수동 가져오기와 게스트 JIT-less 커널 서명 성공이 별개의 경로임을 입증한다.

- 원본 LC 소스 `LCUtils.validateJITLessSetup`은 시험용 dylib를 `ZSigner`로 서명한 후 커널 `checkCodeSignature`를 검사한다. 기존 P78 복구는 `com.SideStore.SideStore` 등의 레거시 generic Keychain `signingCertificate`만 조회하므로 P89가 추가한 원본 SideStore `CertificateManager`의 계정별 활성 P12에 도달하지 못한다. 기존 실패를 타이머·여백·재시도로 처리하지 않는다.

- P91은 기존 P78 후보가 없을 때에만 인증된 SideStore LiveProcess XPC `ScarletNativeCertificateTransport.retrieveSideStoreCertificate()`로 원본 CertificateManager의 **기존** 활성 P12를 조회한다. 저장된 Apple ID 목록은 이전과 이후 두 번 조회하며, **활성 계정 한 개** 및 **호스트 서명 Team에 속한 유일한 계정 한 개**일 때에만 진행한다. 두 Apple ID가 같은 Developer Team이면 자동 교체하지 않는다. 후보 P12가 현재 LC 인증서와 다르고 서명된 호스트 Team과 일치할 때에만 P78의 기존 백업/검증/롤백을 재사용한다. Apple 포털 새 발급, 타 계정 전환, App Group 키 임의 덮어쓰기, 기존 인증서 파기 없음.

- 변경 소스 `rebuild/HostApp/ScarletIntegratedHostView.swift`, `rebuild/Tests/test_v48_r6p91_native_owned_guest_signer.py`, `.github/workflows/scarlet-paired-engines-build.yml`. 정확한 파일·코드 전후 차이와 원격 Git commit SHA들은 append-only `scarlet_remediation_history_appendix.json`의 L150에 기록돼 있다. 기존 P90 계정별 설치 소유권과 UI, P89 인증서 가져오기, V48 화면·회전·멤버십 로직은 변경하지 않았다.

- 신규 소스 계약 테스트 4개 통과는 Xcode 컴파일이나 iPhone JIT-less 성공 증거가 아니다. P91은 빌드 3.8.91·독립 미서명 IPA로 CI를 돌려야 하며, 실기기에서 A→B→A 및 관리 앱 계정 격리, `native_owned_host_team_p12` 복구 시그널과 `signer_recovery_verified`, 실제 게스트 화면/커널 서명, 원본 인증서 미변경 또는 실패 시 롤백을 검증해야 한다. P90의 `no_managed_apps_for_selected_team`은 별도로 등록·소유권 경로 확인이 필요하다.

build(P91): native iOS 27.2 build and separate unsigned release
test(P91): assert native guest signer ownership and reversible recovery
docs(P91): preserve on-device failure evidence and independent native signer recovery handoff

entries.action: P91 adds a unique-account-owned native SideStore certificate lookup after old P78 Keychain candidate exhaustion; reuses original P78 rollback and kernel test, preserving separate Apple ID B signing team, V48 guest geometry and UI.
entries.observation: P90 native CI successful but device guest certificate_invalid/signature_postcheck_invalid persisted. P91 local P91 contracts passed 4 tests; native Xcode and real signed-device recoverability not yet verified.
entries.evidence: P90 3.8.90 session 93bd3576 + pinned LiveContainer LCUtils.validateJITLessSetup source + authenticated SideStore CertificateManager XPC code, full before/after diff.
entries.next_executable_action: Run P91 Xcode27.2 native CI, publish distinct unsigned IPA, then on actual signed phone test A->B->A guest JIT-less code signing and account-owned apps; do not declare success without kernel signature readback and actual guest display.
entries.repeat_policy: No blind P12 replacement, no Team-only ownership inference, no auto portal issuance, no duplicate generic Keychain retry, no guest frame/statusbar changes; failure must restore original AppGroup certificate/password/date.

entries.operation_fingerprint: Restore the real LCJITLessDiagnoseView NavigationLink inside the iOS17+ ScarletSigningReadinessPanel and export its manual test result; separate guest-only locally entitled signer trial from full SideStore refresh prerequisite while retaining reversible kernel validation.
entries.source_behavior_contract: The signed host remains immutable and its Apple Developer Team and accessible App Group must match. The JIT-less diagnostic is visible in the existing native Settings form, its original kernel signing test returns sanitised current-launch JSONL, and candidate-only local recovery does not silently require the stronger installed-app identifier refresh policy. Original transaction rollback remains.

novelty.causal_difference: P7 replaced the entire original iOS17+ LC JIT-less settings section, removing its navigation destination; P91 did not restore it. P91 also gated a host-local signer candidate with canRequestNativeRefresh, a policy that checks an unrelated SideStore signed application identifier; the new path preserves host-team/AppGroup checks but decouples local sign attempts from device refresh readiness.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: P92 JIT-less diagnostic link must appear on iOS27 Settings, open the original native LC screen and record a sanitized manual signature result. On P91 signed host with preflight certificate/team/AppGroup success, signer_recovery_started or an explicit safely classified block must appear after a signature_postcheck_invalid; actual guest success only if kernel postcheck and live guest launch pass.

new_device_evidence.event: jitless_probe_failure_classified/signature_postcheck_invalid without signer_recovery_started and user-reported absent JIT manual diagnostic row
new_device_evidence.observed_value: P91 current session faa1e829 reports four guest launch failures with certificate_invalid and signature_postcheck_invalid; all preflight fields cert/password/team/AppGroup true; no recovery action receipt; original LC diagnostic disappeared from iOS17+ panel.

novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: P78 and P91 focused on candidate P12 sources but left P7 native Settings replacement without a JIT navigation link. P91 introduced a native candidate via XPC but retained canRequestNativeRefresh as a prerequisite for a different local guest signing operation; silent early guards made the failure source invisible.

source_revisions.title: fix(P92): restore original JIT-less diagnostics and decouple guest signer recovery from refresh entitlement gate
test(P92): preserve P78 crash-safe guest signing contract with separate local entitlement gate

entries.action: Restore previously removed original native JIT-less diagnostic NavigationLink in iOS17+ Scarlet signing settings. Record the native manual signature test outcome in Scarlet current-launch JSONL. Repair local guest signer candidate eligibility so it no longer depends on unrelated SideStore device refresh app-identifier check; preserve original signed-host Team/AppGroup and P78 kernel signature rollback.
entries.observation: P91 signed-device session faa1e829 has four certificate_invalid/ signature_postcheck_invalid guest failures and no signer recovery receipts; user cannot find JIT test UI. P92 local Python test suite: 869 run, 866 passed, 3 infrastructure skipped. Native Xcode CI and actual guest launch remain unverified.
entries.evidence: P91 user-supplied current-launch JSONL 2026-11-17 07:45:23Z with exact original LiveContainer JIT view inspected at pinned SHA 9108ae624ea001f7d7696d48407f890b48fa2653; original native Settings integration diff.
entries.next_executable_action: Compile P92 against original LC and SideStore Xcode27.2; check signed device Settings -> JIT-less 진단 -> 원본 테스트 -> 진단 로그 공유. Verify signer_recovery_started / native_signer_recovery_started or explicit reason on P92, then actual kernel-valid guest launch. If signature_postcheck_invalid persists, inspect true native F_ADDFILESIGS and F_CHECK_LV failure mechanisms instead of repeating P12 imports.
entries.repeat_policy: No P12 overwrite without matching Apple team and verified rollback; preserve separate Apple ID account ownership and original V48 guest geometry/status bar. Never treat native CI/ preflight presence as successful signed guest launch.

entries.operation_fingerprint: Read the installed host embedded provisioning profile DeveloperCertificates DER and compare it to the exact X509 certificate extracted from the candidate PKCS12 before any global LiveContainer signer swap.
entries.source_behavior_contract: The selected active Apple ID and host Team still gate XPC; require certificate DER proof against the actual installed host profile even when two accounts share one Team. Never overwrite original P12 on missing proof and retain P78 reversible kernel trial.

novelty.causal_difference: P78 and P91 accepted any same-Team alternate P12 and P91 categorically rejected two accounts sharing one Team. This proposal anchors the same Team candidate to the actual installed host provisioning profile DeveloperCertificates by byte-identical DER before kernel validation, avoiding unrelated certificates from the same Team and allowing a cryptographically evidenced host signer candidate with multiple accounts.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: On a device whose SideStore P12 matches the installed embedded.mobileprovision developer certificate, signer_recovery_trial_started should occur; if no matching private key exists it must explicitly block with a profile mismatch while retaining the original signer, and iOS kernel test remains authoritative.

new_device_evidence.observed_value: signature_postcheck_invalid code 2 repeated with signer_recovery_started 5 and two different account certificate readiness states

novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: P78/P91 and P92 only compared Team OU and registered Apple certificates, not the actual developer certificate authorized by the signed host provisioning profile; P91 also categorically rejected multiple saved owners on one team. P92 iPhone continued kernel code2 despite successful P12 issuance, so this implementation checks host-profile DER provenance before swap.

let options: [String: Any] = [kSecImportExportPassphrase as String: password]
guard SecPKCS12Import(archive as CFData, options as CFDictionary, &decoded)

source_revisions.title: fix(P95): route in-app certificate button through account-owned Apple portal issuer

entries.action: The existing SideStore certificate button now validates one unchanged active AppleID and team, executes original P86 prepare/issue selected Team Apple portal path, revalidates owner, retrieves just-issued or saved native certificate with authenticated XPC, imports only into selected-team store, then invokes original P94 verified host-profile+P78 JITLess recovery. Quota failure and existing cert distinguish from new issue.
entries.observation: Signed-device P94 session 283dc095 confirmed 3.8.94 was installed; guest JIT-less failed signature_postcheck_invalid code2; existing LC signer candidate_not_in_host_profile. The certificate UI recorded provider_origin_checked existing_portal and account_p12_imported ready_existing; this was not new certificate issuance. There is no evidence of successful guest execution.
entries.evidence: User P94 signed-device current-launch 2026-11-17T10:34Z session 283dc095 source fc5613a25976; source P94 button called ScarletNativeCertificateTransport.obtain() backed by global CertificateProvisioningFlow, while P86 independent selected-team native issue path existed but was not called.
entries.next_executable_action: Verify pinned Xcode 27.2 native paired build on branch P95 and release unsigned IPA. On signed iPhone, check native_account_issue_result ready_issued_apple vs ready_existing, current selected Apple-ID owner, host-profile match and JIT-Less kernel postcheck. No proof that Apple can issue if developer certificate quota is exhausted; do not revoke existing certificates. New host certificate requires separately signed host/profile update to avoid guest signer trust mismatch.
entries.repeat_policy: Source fix is UI-to-existing-native-issuer route, not an Apple certificate portal retry or Island layout change. Never delete or revoke certificates or overwrite a different Apple-ID. Signer candidate differing from the installed Scarlet host development profile stays blocked until host is legitimately re-signed and reinstalled without data loss.

entries.operation_fingerprint: On explicit user certificate request require the selected Apple ID owner and Apple portal certificate serial with a matching locally signable private key before reporting reuse; then compare that P12 public DER against the installed host profile to block guest signer trial with a precise error.
entries.source_behavior_contract: Never equate cached certificate expiry with Apple validity, installed host profile trust, or an installed app renewal. Fail closed for mismatched account owner or host signing identity, preserve existing Apple certificates and selected-account XPC storage, and keep kernel test as separate signed-device acceptance.

novelty.causal_difference: L155 connected the button to a prepare-before-issue helper that returns success on a locally non-expired team P12 without Apple portal readback, and L154 still attempts a mismatched host signer. P96 verifies actual portal serial and host profile DER before signaling reuse or guest readiness.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: Signed P96 logs cannot contain native_account_issue_result=ready_existing from only local expiry; valid portal cert reuse reports ready_existing_portal, nonregistered cert must trigger new issue or fail, and host-profile mismatch emits guest signer blocked reason without a kernel trial.
novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: P95 checked only local matching certificate expiry before returning ready_existing; its post-import status said valid even when logged JITLess certificate_invalid and host profile signer mismatch.

## 2026-11-17 P96 / L156 — Apple portal proof and installed-host signer truth

- Signed P95 device log `SourceCommit:9d930382bf1d`, `Build:3.8.95`, session `ae30a2fc`: twice `native_account_issue_result=ready_existing`, but `jitless_host_profile_signer_readback=candidate_not_in_host_profile` and `signature_postcheck_invalid` code2. `sidestore_managed_apps_inspected count=0 reason=no_managed_apps_for_selected_team` blocks APP refresh independently of P12. Account switch verified; later account import blocked, reason redacted, so do not claim which account failed until new visible safe category.

- Code cause: P95 `ensureSelectedTeamCertificate` fast-returns after local OU + X509 expiry `prepare`, before checking Apple's current Developer Portal serial list. It then says an existing valid certificate was reused even when the installed host profile rejects that signer. These are three different states: Apple-registered key, host-signed JIT-Less trust, managed app refresh eligibility.

- P96 functional strategy: explicit existing certificate button directly calls native account-owner-verified `issueInstallCertificate`, where `issue` fetches Apple portal certificate serials BEFORE reusing a cached P12, uses only an unexpired portal-listed serial and matching local private key, or creates a new Apple certificate without revoking existing ones; owner is rechecked across awaits. A successful per-account P12 import checks installed host profile exact X509 DER BEFORE attempting P78 reversible guest-signer recovery. It visibly reports a host re-sign requirement on mismatch, and stops a failed selected-account import before issuing a native provider success receipt. Never conflate `no_managed_apps_for_selected_team` with certificate expiry.

- Maintain V48 UI scale/status bar/Island/switcher/audio, unchanged original Apple IDs, P12 Keychains, bundle ID, and non-destructive updates. No Apple portal account issuance, host re-sign or real iPhone JIT-Less success is verified by Python or Xcode CI.

- New signed-device gates: `native_account_issue_result=ready_existing_portal` only after Apple portal serial match, or `ready_issued_apple` only after actual portal creation. If P12 fails `account_p12_guest_signer_blocked` with `candidate_not_in_host_profile`, re-sign installed host using its exact approved developer certificate/profile; never blindly swap another account's private key. Only `signer_recovery_verified` with kernel success followed by actual guest display can close the guest-launch issue.

entries.operation_fingerprint: Persist Apple ID plus selected Team plus validated Apple developer certificate serial into a separate Keychain service, and select the pinned serial on account switch; only an explicitly requested portal-verified issue or import may bind an unpinned Apple ID, not the active global team key.
entries.source_behavior_contract: An active Apple ID must not inherit the preceding Apple ID native SideStore certificate merely because it shares the same Team OU. New bindings require verified active owner and portal serial and must read back from Keychain. Preserve existing P12 entries and Apple portal records without revocation, guest host profile and JIT-less kernel validation remain independent.

novelty.causal_difference: P90 only verified Team Account database links, P96 checked Apple portal serial but matchingCertificate still looked up any active certificate sharing Team OU; P97 introduces a durable selected-Apple-ID-scoped certificate serial binding and rejects implicit cross-account active-certificate reuse.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: A->B->A switch restores the serial pinned to A, B with no pin reports missing instead of choosing A by OU alone, explicit Apple portal issue/import binds B only after owner and serial are verified. Existing unrelated keys remain untouched.
novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: Previous code uses matchingCertificate(for teamID) across all native operations, and account rows display certificate readiness based on a team match, which can select another Apple ID current certificate when both share Team ID.

- Signed-device P96 source commit `920732fe2da3`, build `3.8.96`, session `6fffed84`: current guest launch JIT-Less `signature_postcheck_invalid`, installed profile existing signer `candidate_not_in_host_profile`; target native refresh `no_managed_apps_for_selected_team`, and two selected accounts may share a Team ID with native global active P12. source_revisions.title: P97 account-keychain signing identity isolation

entries.operation_fingerprint: Route the existing user-facing SideStore Certificate Get button via a new account/team-verified native XPC method that directly invokes Apple DeveloperPortalProxy.createCertificate, without consulting the existing active or portal signable P12 as a replacement and without revoking certificates; assert actual new serial readback.
entries.source_behavior_contract: The manual button means NEW Apple certificate issuance. Apple 7460/quota and network errors are reported as failures and may never silently become successful reuse. Existing account switching, background refresh and import keep their non-destructive reuse semantics. New issue requires verified owner on both sides, issued cert owner+expiry and newly created Apple portal serial readback before reporting success.

novelty.causal_difference: L155 and L156 connected certificate button to issueInstallCertificate but the implementation returned ready_existing_portal when local or Apple portal valid cert existed. L157 scoped certificate serials to Apple IDs but still did not change the explicit manual operation to force fresh issuance. L158 adds a distinct user-requested force-fresh operation, retaining reuse for other app installs.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: Tapping the existing certificate get button invokes scarletIssueFreshInstallTeamCertificate and createCertificate without a preemptive existing-certificate return. A full Apple portal quota causes explicit selected_team_certificate_quota_reached and never ready_existing_portal; new serial verified after issuance returns ready_issued_apple.
novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: P97 still maps manual UI to issueInstallCertificate and issue(teamID:) which reuses portal valid keys and yields ready_existing_portal before calling Apple createCertificate; it does not implement a new-certificate-only request.

## 2026-11-17 P98 / L158 — Manual certificate receive MUST request fresh Apple issue

- User-observed P95-P97 defect: tapping `SideStore 인증서 받기` returns `ready_existing_portal` and reuses old valid P12, even though the action is meant to obtain a newly issued Apple developer signing certificate. Earlier changes validated reused certificates but did not alter the operation semantics.

- P98 functional source fix: keep native install/auth reuse untouched. Add separate authenticated XPC protocol/worker method `scarletIssueFreshInstallTeamCertificate` -> `ScarletGuestSignInAgent.issueFreshInstallTeamCertificate` -> `ScarletInstallTeamAuthority.issue(teamID:forceNew:true)`. Explicit fresh bypasses both preexisting active certificate and portal signable-P12 loops, directly calls `DeveloperPortalProxy.shared.createCertificate`, validates Team/expiry and new serial distinct from pre-request portal, binds it to the selected active Apple ID/Team, then reads Apple portal again and only returns `ready_issued_apple` on verified registration. A 7460 quota error is FAILURE, never silently reused; other Apple certificates are never revoked or deleted.

- The existing manual button retains its location, label and accessibility identifier but now calls `ScarletNativeSavedAccounts.issueFreshInstallCertificate` and accepts ONLY `ready_issued_apple`. Messages distinguish quota, unconfirmed issue and successfully new issued certificate. An imported just-issued P12 already active in the native Keychain is logged as `new_apple_p12_already_active_in_native_store` rather than mislabeling the issue operation reused. Preserve specific host-profile mismatch UI even if later SideStore inspection is unready.

- Verification: source gate and Python contracts are NOT signed-device proof; only an actual Apple portal transaction with new serial and successful host profile/kernel checks can prove functional end-to-end success. entries.operation_fingerprint: Reject SideStore globally unique CoreData Account identifier and Team identifier collisions across different Apple IDs before updating any account record or mutating active state; read back precise Apple ID and Team relationship, retrieve per-account signer pin and InstalledApp count and show in existing settings rows. Distinguish original refresh zero-target states and Apple portal issuance error stages without altering P101 LC signer.
entries.source_behavior_contract: P102 will never overwrite a prior Apple ID account record, silently steal a Team row, copy A's installed apps or report a different account as signature ready based on a matching Team ID alone. Native SideStore unique Team identifier prevents independent CoreData Team rows when two Apple IDs share the same Team; the code must report a collision instead of claiming independent management. Existing JIT-less guest signer and UI layout remain untouched.

novelty.causal_difference: P90 introduced Apple-ID-plus-Team ownership checks only in downstream native install/refresh paths; P101 repaired guest signer expiration. Neither guarded the upstream SideStore ensureActiveTeamForRefresh persistent CoreData Account.first(identifier) and Team.first(identifier) operations, which could overwrite Account.appleID or reuse Team from another Apple ID before downstream validations. P102 changes that actual mutation precondition and adds per-owner UI, issuing and inventory provenance, not another profile/guest resize or cache retry.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: For two Apple ID accounts with distinct verified Team identities, A to B to A will produce separate account-email, signed-certificate and managed-app rows; when Account or Team identifiers are globally shared by different owners, new source refuses cross-owner overwrite and reports exact collision. An actual iPhone log must prove account ID and Team readback, not just successful switching.
novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: P97 signer pin separates account certificate in Keychain but does not stop SideStore CoreData registration from changing Apple ID on a globally selected Account/Team row. P100 XPC rebind and P101 LC signer validity did not touch these native CoreData mutations or count per-owner InstalledApps.

# Scarlet Crystal P102 — 계정별 소유권·인증서 오류·갱신 대상 분리
- 사용자 제공 P101 실기기: certificate_bridge_imported, signature_valid, 게스트 PID 834 화면 연결, 계정 전환 4회, 오디오 재개·정지 응답 ok.
- 미해결: 두 로그인 계정의 소유권/표시 구분, 신규 Apple 인증서 발급 4회 실패, 관리 앱 0개, 위험 컨트롤 5개와 상태바 숨김.
- P101 로그는 로그인 성공 근거이지 계정별 앱·인증서 소유권 격리 근거는 아니다.
1. ScarletGuestSignInAgent.ensureActiveTeamForRefresh는 원본 CoreData에서 Account.identifier와 Team.identifier만으로 객체를 찾고 기존 Account.appleID를 새 이메일로 덮어쓸 수 있었다. Team.account 관계 일치 검증도 빠져 있었다.
2. 원본 SideStore AltStore 17_7 데이터 모델은 Account.identifier, Team.identifier 각각 전역 고유키를 사용한다. 따라서 서로 다른 Apple ID가 하나의 Team ID를 공유하면 Team을 2개 독립 객체로 만들 수 없다. 조용히 Team을 이전 계정에서 새 계정으로 재귀속하면 관리 앱까지 섞인다.
3. Settings의 인증서 준비 확인은 Team ID만 비교해 같은 Team 소속의 다른 Apple ID를 구별하지 못했다.
4. 설정의 Apple 계정 목록은 이메일/활성 상태만 보여주고 관리 앱과 인증서의 독립 소유권을 표시하지 않았다.
5. 원본 SideStore fetchAppsForRefreshingAll은 비활성 앱 등을 필터링하므로 반환 0건만으로 DB 미등록을 확정할 수 없다.
- Apple ID와 Team의 실제 CoreData 관계 및 저장된 Keychain 로그인 ID/토큰을 전환 후 재검증한다. 서로 다른 Apple ID에 동일한 계정/Team 고유 객체가 연결되면 명시적으로 차단한다.
- 계정별 관리 앱 수는 원본 CoreData InstalledApp.team.account와 정확한 Apple ID+Team 조합으로 집계한다. 계정별 원본 서명 인증서의 저장·유효성도 별도 확인한다.
- 설정 및 로그인 화면의 기존 계정 행 안에 이메일, Team, 서명 인증서 상태 및 관리 앱 수를 각각 보여준다. 불필요한 섹션·구분선은 늘리지 않는다.
- Apple 포털 신규 인증서 발급 오류 단계(preflight/create/readback/import_lookup), NSError 도메인/코드/원인 코드를 안전한 XPC 진단 필드로 남긴다. 사용자 계정 ID, P12, 암호, 토큰, Apple 응답 문자열을 기록하지 않는다.
- 갱신 대상 0건을 실제 미등록, 모두 비활성, 원본 갱신 필터 제외, DB 조회 실패로 구분한다.
- P101 게스트 서명·커널 검증·화면 연결·멀티태스킹·오디오·상태바 위험 방어 정책은 변경하지 않는다.

2. 계정 B가 계정 A의 관리 앱·인증서를 소유한 것처럼 표시되거나 재서명하지 않아야 한다.
3. 두 Apple ID의 Team ID가 동일하면 원본 SideStore DB의 고유키 충돌을 분명히 표시하고 다른 계정 Team/InstalledApp을 덮어쓰지 않는다. 이 경우 완전 분리에는 원본 CoreData 스키마·마이그레이션 변경이 필요하다.

entries.operation_fingerprint: On successful explicit selected Apple ID and Team P12 import, if its X509 is absent from the currently installed host provisioning profile, dispatch a dedicated authenticated XPC operation that selects only the actual installed Scarlet .app, verifies existing host signing team and selected Apple ID+Team local signer identity, runs upstream native AppManager.install to re-sign all host extensions under the chosen certificate, then preserves pending installed profile change readback across relaunch; no other managed apps are selected.
entries.source_behavior_contract: Never insert new P12 as usable LC guest signer until installed host profile DER matches after native installer and reversible validation. Do not cross Team IDs or silently revoke existing keys, delete existing apps, change account identity, install an untrusted source URL or claim iPhone installation without real profile readback. Original auto refresh and manual refresh remain intact.

novelty.causal_difference: P106 made a manual zero-ManagedApp fallback but no code connects the successful P12-import event to a host re-sign request, and P107 only preserved failure response strings. The P107 on-device log shows P12 import succeeded ready_existing, then only candidate_not_in_host_profile; P108 calls a distinct native host-only transaction even if other managed apps exist.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: After explicit P12 import when candidate DER differs from installed host DeveloperCertificates and current account Team owns the original host .app, the LiveProcess invokes original AppManager.install with the selected account signing certificate and the original four host extension profiles; a different host Team is rejected, background is unchanged, and the next device process verifies updated embedded.mobileprovision and installed signer DER.

entries.repeat_policy: No fake app installation status from callback, no guest LC signer bridging before installed host provisioning profile cert matches, no foreign-team ownership adoption, no background replacement, no revocation or Keychain deletion, do not alter dynamic island and multitasking.

entries.operation_fingerprint: The P108 host sends its exact selected Apple ID and Team ID to SideStoreSupport XPC and the native worker instead of re-reading only global mutable active ownership; the worker requires the same active account and Team both before and after signing, verifies the owner-pinned serial equals the active signing certificate after prepare and after the device transport await, and rejects an unauthorized or changed owner without mutating another account.

novelty.causal_difference: P108 added a host-only AppManager.install but its XPC request carried only a host path, allowing the asynchronous worker to derive a different global account/team from a later activation. P109 sends expected identity through the actual XPC invocation and validates native active signing serial around the native installer, rather than merely verifying one active account in the host UI.

entries.repeat_policy: Change release job allowlist only; no signing, installed host or guest runtime tweaks; report GitHub release asset only after API readback and never report Apple code-signed/installed iPhone result.

entries.operation_fingerprint: Restore original SwiftUI native top scroll-edge gradient only inside the nested LC JIT-less and entitlement Forms by no longer disabling the top edge treatment in the diagnostic scroll helper. Move the two long JITless host bundle and App Group identifiers from cramped trailing HStack values to full-width multiline native Form rows; preserve all native Apple entitlement and JITLess test logic untouched.
entries.source_behavior_contract: Do not change host/guest safe-area metrics, overlay masking, resident FBScene content window, native status-bar ownership, signing certificate materials, account switching, Apple portal issuer, SideStore refresh or installed host identity. Limit the change to original JITless diagnostic Forms and validate compiled original test route remains unmodified.

novelty.causal_difference: P109 signed device shows content of a pushed native JITless Form visible behind top status clock and navigation bar. The existing modifier deliberately disables all system scroll-edge effects in the *diagnostic Form*, including its native top content fade; restoring the top native effect is not a guest viewport/safe-area/statusbar masking method. Long host IDs are constrained to trailing HStack column and should occupy their own Form row.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: After native JITless screen scrolls upward, account/host field rows no longer remain fully legible behind the native top title/status bar, while the original native JITless test still reports success and Form fields render long identifiers without narrow trailing word-by-word wrapping. No Guest/Island layout or certificate state changes.

entries.operation_fingerprint: At real manual zero-managed-host native install and regular team-filtered AppManager refresh, snapshot the selected Apple ID/Team and active Keychain signer serial across RSD awaits and stop before dispatch on mismatch; patch upstream profile ID creation to append the selected team only when absent.
entries.source_behavior_contract: Only the selected account and pinned serial may reach original AppManager manual/background signing; no foreign-Team migration, no CoreData takeover or P12 deletion; original installed preferred bundle identifiers remain intact but future same-Team provisioning avoids Team.Team duplication.

source_revisions.title: fix(P113): fence selected-account signer across native renewal and avoid repeated Team suffix

entries.observation: P112 real iPhone current session dd52f38c reported zero managed refresh targets and host_managed_owner_mismatch. P113 source pins account-team-certificate serial across transport before both regular and manual fallback native AppManager requests; base Team-suffixed App ID is no longer suffixed twice when no prior preferred installed ID exists. P113 local Python suite: 975 tests, 4 skipped, no failures; native build and signed device still need validation.
entries.action: Wire idempotent selected Team suffix into pinned original SideStore FetchProvisioningProfilesOperation via generator; put strict Apple ID/Team/P12 serial post-transport identity guard in previously unfenced regular automatic/manual refresh and zero-managed manual host fallback. Keep original Apple-signed host ID, existing previously duplicated signed IDs, SideStore App Group, all extensions, certs and credentials unchanged.
entries.repeat_policy: Never overwrite original installed identities or migrate app data on selected account change; refuse changed signer before SideStore AppManager, no false install success. Apple device end-to-end remains unverified.

novelty.causal_difference: P113 only fences refresh against an already pinned signer and patches one suffix; it lacks R112 owner-key recovery, selects the first matching Team CoreData ID even for another Apple ID and shares a host-Team IPA inbox; P114 repairs these separate persistent-state compatibility boundaries.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: An R112 device with exactly one unambiguous portal-registered signable legacy certificate can bind its existing key non-destructively; two accounts sharing Team cannot hijack an unowned certificate; existing deployed IDs retain their exact identity; scoped staging rejects a foreign account.
novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: R113 uses pinnedSignerSerial without an R112 migration reader; matchingCertificate returns nil for a pre-P113 legacy Keychain record and the .hasSuffix check ignores prior Team.Team data. Its shared staging directory has no Apple ID owner.

source_revisions.title: fix(R6P115): reconcile signed host CoreData owner only with pinned certificate proof

entries.observation: R114 signed iPhone log recorded host_managed_owner_mismatch after A-B switch. P115 adds conditional source fix with four new source contract tests; Python full suite 984 tests OK with 4 skips. No claim that this signed-device runtime path was executed or that Apple portal code20, Dynamic Island overlap or visual statusbar were repaired.
entries.action: Build on Xcode 27.2 GitHub Actions and test B signed host with B owned signer against stale singleton CoreData row. Verify AppManager refresh, strict owner failure paths, and A-B-A across active guest; separately investigate Apple portal code20 and guest Island via new scene creation root cause.
entries.repeat_policy: No repeat of P84 blocked Island layout/statusbar/inset/masking methods. Do not label Python tests, native CI or unsigned IPA as signed-device success.

entries.operation_fingerprint: Parent both resident controllers before first loading their views, acknowledge the inner mounted child with UIKit didMoveToParentViewController, and revoke readiness before removing that exact owned child on exit.
entries.source_behavior_contract: Use public UIKit controller containment on the resident host main thread. An attached scene is render-ready only if it is the same mounted child whose didMove has completed. Keep the original nonresident and legacy setup and exit paths.

novelty.causal_difference: L033 and L043 gated remote readiness or deferred the outer extension launch. Neither established the inner controller parent before first view access, completed its UIKit didMove callback, or detached it before host invalidation.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: The generated resident controller acquires its parent before first view access and reports ready only after didMove. If unsafe foreground controls persist when this contract holds on the signed same-device A/B run, the visual hypothesis is falsified.
novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: Host and root already report the expected safe area while a guest still has interactive content at the top edge. Earlier owner-layout, status-bar and wait-for-surface changes cannot supply a missing UIViewController containment callback.

normal_experimental_diff.normal_mode_source: ScarletIntegratedHostView.swift selects app.runApp(multitask: false) on iPhone. Pinned LiveContainer 9108ae624ea0 LCAppModel.runApp transfers to launchToGuestApp without the nested resident container.
normal_experimental_diff.resident_mode_source: ScarletFullscreenSceneViewport.reconcile loads the outer view before adding the child. Pinned MultitaskSupport/AppSceneViewController.m setUpAppPresenter loads the inner controller view before parenting it and never calls didMoveToParentViewController after mounting.
normal_experimental_diff.proven_difference: The normal phone launch uses the original process handoff. Only the resident render path requires this custom nested parent-child lifecycle; its previous receipt accepted a view/superview match without a completed child transition.
normal_experimental_diff.failure_causal_link: The missing UIKit lifecycle notification is present in the render code and can affect initialization of a controller that depends on its installed owner. Existing device evidence establishes the residual collision, not that repairing containment eliminates it.

alternative_strategies.reason_not_selected: Selected. The pinned modern presenter omits a required UIKit callback; source and signed-device criteria can test this independently of geometric policy. L033 observed attachment and L043 only parented the outer host before starting the extension.

L042 already considered scene-manifest policies. Another correctly laid-out guest in this session has the same lack of a manifest, so changing manifests or launch policy has no discriminating support.
L024 addressed scene ownership. Existing receipts show multiple individually owned and attached remote processes with distinct outcomes, with no evidence of presenting the wrong process.
L100/L101 changed local layout writers. Neither the redacted samples nor the original host sources identify an erroneous application-specific writer whose contract can be safely replaced.

entries.new_source_root_cause: The resident UI can consider an onscreen view render-ready without ever calling didMoveToParentViewController on its nested scene controller. The pinned code also invalidates the hosting owner before looking up the child for removal.
entries.runtime_acceptance_gate: On the same signed iPhone and guest compare OFF/ON cold launch. Require no overlapping controls and visible native clock/battery, verify top-control hit testing, full scroll and portrait/landscape, return from Home and A-B-A with the same live PID. A repeat of the residual controls rejects the visual hypothesis.
entries.observation: A prior signed launch recorded a residual top-edge collision in one of several resident guests despite an already-correct root safe area. There is no same-session OFF sample or signed run of this repair. The pinned P115 generated controller fails all three attachment/removal checks; the P116 generated target passes them. The Linux suite ran 988 tests with seven skipped. No native or signed-device result is available for this revision.
entries.action: Validate the native archive and signed-device acceptance gate. Treat the separate saved-pairing transport deferrals as unresolved pending independent evidence.
entries.repeat_policy: Use the existing P84 family gate for later changes and retain every prior receipt.

source_revisions.title: fix(R6P116): complete resident scene child containment before reveal

entries.hypothesis: The missing resident child transition may prevent a guest layout that depends on its controller hierarchy from following the original full-screen launch. This has a reproducible source failure; whether the visual symptom shares that cause requires a signed same-guest device run.
generated_runtime_targets_if_integrated: MultitaskSupport/AppSceneViewController.m (resident UIKit setup, render readiness and cleanup)

entries.operation_fingerprint: In the registered host scene diff callback, compare old and new host values, apply only changed lifecycle, orientation and interface style fields to a copy of the receiving guest's settings, then forward that copy with the original filtered transition context.
entries.source_behavior_contract: A resident must retain its own scene persistence identifier and other remote settings when its host window changes. The callback requires the live controller's attached host scene and an available remote settings snapshot. The original callback remains the delegate path for other controllers.

novelty.causal_difference: L182 completed UIKit child containment. L024 introduced a host for resident scenes and L043 delayed extension startup. None isolates subsequent host settings transactions from each guest's own state.
novelty.falsifiable_prediction: Give two guests different scene identities and inject an unrelated host change. P116 forwards the host identity to both. P117 must retain both original identities and forward only effective lifecycle, rotation or style changes. Persistent overlap with that contract rejects the visual hypothesis.
novelty.why_prior_fix_failed: The signed P116 run shows both remote surfaces attached. One guest still reports eight overlapping controls after its host crossed background and foreground, despite the root receiving the expected top guide.

normal_experimental_diff.normal_mode_source: ScarletIntegratedHostView on iPhone calls app.runApp(multitask: false). Pinned LCAppModel.runApp dispatches launchToGuestApp. No Scarlet controller registers for another window's settings in that path.
normal_experimental_diff.resident_mode_source: Pinned LiveContainer 9108ae624ea0 MultitaskSupport/AppSceneViewController.m sets persistenceIdentifier to dataUUID, registers for host-window diffs, and computes baseSettings from the old host settings. ScarletFullscreenSceneStack.appSceneVC(_:didUpdateFrom:transitionContext:lifecycleActionType:) sends that entire object to the guest presenter.
normal_experimental_diff.proven_difference: The separate resident host can replace a guest's private scene state on an unrelated host transition. In the failing P116 guest, the host went inactive/background before the 650 ms scan and returned active before the 2600 ms scan. The other guest had no recorded host background transition during its samples.
normal_experimental_diff.failure_causal_link: The receiving object and incoming settings have different owners in pinned source. Changes in effective guest presentation state are a testable contributor to the layout symptom. There is no on-device readback of the raw settings transaction or same-guest mode-OFF sample in this report.

alternative_strategies.reason_not_selected: Selected. The host-to-guest whole-settings assignment has a deterministic identity-clobbering input. Compare two independent guest snapshots to the same host transition and verify per-guest values and legitimate lifecycle changes.

The failing guest has no scene manifest, the other does, and the SDK overrides also differ. The installed log shows each actual post-swap manifest matches its own guest. Changing guest launch policy on these two samples would confound app identity. L040/L042/L046 already cover launch and SDK behavior.

The failing guest's own header stays at y=0 before older reflow trials and both trials roll back. The closed-source view-level writer is not identified. Changing header layout would repeat L100/L101 and risk touch and scrolling.
L182 already completed containment. Both P116 guests report an attached remote surface. Repeating containment or altering its timing would not isolate the settings-copy defect.

entries.new_source_root_cause: The Swift resident scene delegate submits a complete snapshot derived from AppSceneViewController's host UIWindowScene to a different FBScene. Source reproduction can replace the receiving guest's persistence identity even when the host changed only foreground state.
entries.runtime_acceptance_gate: On the same signed phone and same guest, compare OFF and ON with and without a host background/foreground cycle. Require zero visible overlapping controls, visible native clock and battery, correct top hit targets, full scroll, portrait/landscape, Home return and A-to-B-to-A with retained PIDs. Repeated overlap rejects this visual hypothesis.
entries.observation: Signed P116 recorded a 62 pt root guide for both guests. The first guest had eight visible unsafe controls (first y=3) and seven images at both 650 and 2600 ms, including after host foreground entry. Earlier layout trials reverted. The second guest had zero unsafe controls and one image at both samples. Automatic refresh separately reported host_managed_owner_mismatch twice.
entries.action: Build an unsigned P117 archive, verify its embedded audit and build identity, then evaluate the signed-device acceptance gate. Preserve the independent managed-owner failure for its own investigation.
entries.repeat_policy: Retain all previous history. A later Island repair must use a distinct operational family; no new log or version waives the gate.
entries.hypothesis: Changes made by the host scene may account for remaining resident guest layout differences. The signed P116 log demonstrates the symptom and lifecycle sequence, not a causal connection or a P117 outcome.
